question: Let \(f\) be a function such that \(f''(x)\) exists, and \(f''(x)>0\) for all \(x\in[a,b]\). For any point \(c\in[a,b]\), let \(A(c)\) denote the area of the region bounded by \(y=f(x)\), the tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=c\) and the lines \(x=a\) and \(x=b\). Then

options.A: \(A(c)\) attains its minimum at \(c=\frac12(a+b)\) for any such \(f\)
options.B: \(A(c)\) attains its maximum at \(c=\frac12(a+b)\) for any such \(f\)
options.C: \(A(c)\) attains its minimum at both \(c=a\) and \(c=b\) for any such \(f\)
options.D: the points \(c\) where \(A(c)\) attains its minimum depend on \(f\).
